---
title: "Part 2 — Building (Modules 2–4; Module 5 pending)"
---

Part 2 walks you from defining one capsule, through implementing and
testing it, to composing a minimal Pico and resolving its capability
requirement by hand against the installed capsule. Modules 2–4 are
runnable today against the **adopted v0.1 capsule contract** in
[`open-engineering-capsules/source`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/tree/bf071c2c1b57)
at pinned commit `bf071c2c1b57`
([`memo1.md`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo1.md),
[`memo2.md`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo2.md)).
Module 5 remains deferred — see below.

## Modules 2–4 (available)

Each module pairs a lesson under `part-2/` with the matching steps of
the shared [`labs/greeting-capsule/`](../../../labs/greeting-capsule/)
lab:

- **Module 2 — [Define a capsule](01-define-a-capsule/index.qmd)** —
  capsule metadata and contract boundaries against the adopted v0.1
  capsule contract. Pairs with
  [`labs/greeting-capsule/`](../../../labs/greeting-capsule/) Steps
  1–3 (fetch upstream artefacts, author `solution/capsule.yaml`,
  JSON-Schema validate).
- **Module 3 — [Implement and test a capsule](02-implement-and-test-a-capsule/index.qmd)** —
  implement `oe.greeting` behind the capsule contract in stdlib
  Python, keep dependencies local to the implementation, and cover
  the code with unit and contract tests. Pairs with
  [`labs/greeting-capsule/`](../../../labs/greeting-capsule/) Steps
  4–5.
- **Module 4 — [Compose a Pico](03-compose-a-pico/index.qmd)** —
  declarative capability composition under memo2 §2 D2 / §3 D3 / §4
  D4; compose a minimal Pico and resolve `spec.capabilities` by hand
  against the installed capsule in the shape of upstream
  `fixtures/scenarios/resolve-greeting.yaml`. Pairs with
  [`labs/greeting-capsule/`](../../../labs/greeting-capsule/) Steps
  6–7.

## Module 5 (deferred)

**Module 5 — Run and inspect the Pico** is **not yet available**: it
waits on a capsule-aware runtime (`open-engineering-picos/source` is
memo-only) and memo2 §5 follow-up (b) (the reference capability
resolver). Until those ship,
[`labs/hello-pico/`](../../../labs/hello-pico/) remains the run path
(partially covered by hello-pico, per
[`memo23.md`](../../../memo23.md) §9 step 3). This course will consume
the upstream runtime and resolver when they publish; it does not
define a second, course-specific one
([`memo23.md`](../../../memo23.md) §3.2).

## Part 2 prerequisites

- A working shell and text editor; Python 3.8+ on `PATH`.
- `jsonschema` and `pyyaml` installed for the lab's schema and shape
  checks: `python3 -m pip install --user jsonschema pyyaml`.
- `curl` on `PATH` (the lab's `solution/fetch-upstream.sh` falls back
  to `gh api` only when `curl` is denied by the upstream private
  repository).
- Completed [Part 1 · Understand a Pico](../part-1/01-introduction/index.qmd).

## Pinned upstream commit

Everything Part 2 fetches, quotes, or links from the capsule
contract repository is pinned at
[`bf071c2c1b57`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/tree/bf071c2c1b57).
The lab's `solution/fetch-upstream.sh` script downloads the normative
`capsule.schema.json` and the ten `fixtures/scenarios/*.yaml` from
that commit into the untracked `labs/greeting-capsule/build/upstream/`
directory; no schema or resolver is vendored into the Academy tree.

See the [course overview](../index.qmd) for the six-module course
spine and the zero-optional-platform path.
